drivingQuestion: What distinguishes the mishna's permission to sons/brothers from the rule of one suspected with a woman?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is answered in the next unit.

segments.he: וְכוּלָּן מוּתָּרוֹת לִבְנֵיהֶם אוֹ לַאֲחֵיהֶם. מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן: הַנִּטְעָן מִן הָאִשָּׁה, אָסוּר בְּאִמָּהּ וּבְבִתָּהּ וּבַאֲחוֹתָהּ.
segments.en: § The mishna taught: «And all of these» women who were prohibited from marrying the man who freed them due to some suspicion «are permitted to the sons or to the brothers» of those who set them free. The Gemara asks: In «what» way «is» this case «different from that which we learned» in the Tosefta (4:5) that «one suspected» of adultery «with» a specific «woman is prohibited» not only from marrying her, but also «from» marrying «her mother, and her daughter, and her sister.» Yet here we allow his sons and brothers to marry the woman despite the suspicion.
